about_description: Me away from code: where I live, what I love and what makes me who I am.
about_intro_place: My roots are in Trabzon; I was born and raised in Istanbul. I love Istanbul, though it is neither heaven nor hell; a strange mix of the two, at most. To get away from its chaos, its noise and its traffic, I moved to Sakarya, and now I live a quiet life in the middle of a forest, waking up to birdsong.
about_intro_character: I love research and learning new things; my mind is always busy making something. Helping people, and touching their lives even in a small way, feels good. I also enjoy thinking something through from scratch, designing it, setting its strategy and running it with every piece in view. And I can't do without order: I file my photo archive city by city, neighborhood by neighborhood, so I can find any shot in seconds; even the books on my shelves are arranged by period.
about_intro_roots: I am attached to my roots and my culture. I love the age-old heritage, the traditions and the subtleties of these lands; knowing this heritage and keeping it alive matters to me.
about_intro_contact: If you want to say hello, <mail>write to me</mail>.

about_walks_body: I like to see more than a city's famous spots: its back streets, its cafés, its corner shops and its people. That is how I have walked through many of Istanbul's neighborhoods, one step at a time. What began as a way to get moving after long days at a desk soon grew into many kilometers, and brought new people and friendships along the way.
about_walks_body_photos: I came to love taking photos on these walks, and I share them on Instagram. I also sort the places I visit into themed, public lists on Google Maps, so others can discover them too.

about_books_body: I love collecting books; buying one, finding it a place on the shelf and reading it are each a pleasure of their own. I am drawn most to Islam, Sufism, and Ottoman and Roman history. The bookcase at home has grown over the years, and I keep a list of what is in it on the Library page.

virastack_description: Headless, type-safe tools and agent rules for building modern React apps.
virastack_problem_body_1: AI made writing code faster, but speed has a cost. Without a solid foundation every agent goes its own way, and technical debt, performance losses and accessibility gaps pile up quietly.
virastack_problem_body_2: ViraStack lays that foundation on day one: a set architecture, rules that explain it to your agents, and ready-made hooks for the parts of a form you keep rewriting.
virastack_layer_learn_lead: You can't build on a foundation you don't know. Academy teaches frontend in order, and Guide shows how a modern web app is built in three minutes.
virastack_layer_start_lead: One command to a type-safe Next.js or TanStack Start project, with architecture rules already written for your agents.
virastack_layer_build_lead: Headless, type-safe form hooks that render nothing. Install each on its own, use them together in one React Hook Form, and run the same rules on the server.
virastack_principle_headless_body: <mask>Mask</mask>, <password>Password</password> and <address>Address</address> draw no UI. Inputs, components and styles stay yours; the hook only brings the behavior.
virastack_principle_typesafe_body: <start>Start</start> ships with strict TypeScript and Zod, and every package carries its own types. <mask>Mask</mask> and <address>Address</address> check field names against your form's type, so a typo fails at compile time.
virastack_principle_agents_body: The same architecture rules are written for Claude Code, Cursor and any agent that reads AGENTS.md, each in its tool's own format. Agents write code that fits your project.
virastack_principle_independent_body: MIT licensed, free, with no paid tiers. Each package is versioned on its own, and using one never pulls in the others.
virastack_powered_by_lead: ViraStack doesn't replace these tools; it sets them up to work together.
virastack_why_body_1: For years I've turned what I learn into projects; the first was Turkuaz, which I wrote to understand CSS in depth. Today that curiosity lives on in ViraStack: <start>Start</start> sets up the project architecture, <ai>AI</ai> writes the agent rules, and <mask>Mask</mask>, <password>Password</password> and <address>Address</address> handle the forms, all to one shared standard.
virastack_why_body_2: I like getting into the kitchen of a craft and owning its quality end to end; ViraStack is my attempt to turn that into something anyone can use for free. I tell the whole story in <post>ViraStack: Frontend Ecosystem</post> (in Turkish).
virastack_status_body: Each product is versioned on its own and grows with feedback from the community. Reporting a bug, suggesting an idea or leaving a star on GitHub helps the most.
